content: Take dexlansoprazole exactly as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep dexlansoprazole out of the reach of children. Do not chew, cut, or crush the capsules. You can take dexlansoprazole with or without food. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents on one tablespoon of applesauce. Swallow the applesauce immediately without chewing. Do not mix the contents with any other food. If dexlansoprazole is administered through a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow the instructions provided by your healthcare provider. This medication is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn. It may take 1 to 4 days to achieve its full effect. Children under 2 years of age may be at greater risk for certain side effects. Discuss the risks with your healthcare provider if your child is under 2 years old. Before Using Dexlansoprazole: Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This helps determine if dexlansoprazole is appropriate for you. Notify your provider if you have any of the following conditions: Low blood potassium (hypokalemia) Low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia) Low blood calcium (hypocalcemia) Low blood sodium (hyponatremia) Liver problems Drug Interactions: Dexlansoprazole may interact with other medications and supplements. Always inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using. Specific medications to discuss include: Methotrexate Digoxin (used for irregular heartbeat and heart failure) Warfarin (a blood thinner) Tacrolimus (used to prevent organ transplant rejection) Certain antiretroviral medications for HIV/AIDS (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir) St. John’s Wort Rifampin (used for tuberculosis) Some medications may alter the blood levels of dexlansoprazole or vice versa. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if dexlansoprazole affects pregnancy or harms an unborn baby. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is also unknown if dexlansoprazole passes into breast milk. Notify your provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much dexlansoprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects include: Diarrhea Stomach pain Nausea Symptoms of the common cold Vomiting Gas Headache (in children aged 12 to 17 years) Sore throat (in children aged 12 to 17 years) Contact your healthcare provider if these side effects bother you. Serious Side Effects: Kidney Problems: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis may occur at any time during treatment. Contact your doctor immediately if you notice decreased urine output or blood in your urine. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your provider immediately if these occur. Severe Skin Reactions: Rare but serious conditions like Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) can occur. Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rash, blisters, or watery eyes. Stop the medication and seek emergency help if these symptoms develop. DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms): This multi-organ hypersensitivity reaction can affect the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin/eyes. Stop the medication and seek immediate medical attention. Lupus: Dexlansoprazole may cause or worsen lupus, an autoimmune disorder. Notify your provider if you experience new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. Vitamin B-12 Deficiency: Long-term use (3 years or more) may reduce vitamin B-12 absorption, leading to symptoms like a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling in the hands or feet. Hypomagnesemia: Low magnesium levels can cause seizures, heart rhythm problems, dizziness, muscle spasms, or changes in heart rate. Long-term use or concurrent use of other medications that lower magnesium increases this risk. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term or high-dose use may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults. Precautions: Do not use dexlansoprazole if you are allergic to any of its ingredients, including other proton pump inhibitors. Always consult your pharmacist or healthcare provider for a complete list of ingredients in the specific product you are using. Avoid taking dexlansoprazole with certain medications unless approved by your healthcare provider. Additional Notes: Dexlansoprazole does not have known interactions with food or drinks, but it is unclear if alcohol affects its efficacy. Always consult your healthcare provider for any concerns or questions about this medication.
